key_insight: A transferred monolayer graphene contact improves AlInN/Si solar cell performance by boosting current collection and fill factor without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, transparent conductive contact that can enhance nitride-based photovoltaic device efficiency while remaining compatible with heterostructure integration on Si.
method: Built AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with an a-Si buffer layer.
Studied three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact.
evidence_signal: Under illumination and dark testing, graphene-enabled devices showed higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and overall power conversion efficiency across all compositions, while open-circuit voltage stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the quality, uniformity, and contact resistance of the transferred graphene layer, which may affect scalability and reproducibility.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
